pages.title: Frederick C. Robie House
pages.tagline: A measured survey of a long, low house in Hyde Park, Chicago

pages.title: Every line runs with the street
pages.text: A long, low house on a corner lot in Chicago's Hyde Park: two slipped rectangular volumes under broad hipped roofs. The living and dining rooms are raised to the second floor and opened to the street through a continuous band of art-glass doors. The roofs cantilever far beyond the walls, and the brick is laid with raked horizontal joints, so every line of the house runs with the street.

pages.title: One continuous living and dining space
pages.caption: Second (main) floor plan, 1/8 inch to the foot: one continuous living and dining space divided only by the central fireplace and stair; guest room, kitchen and servants' rooms along the north wing.

pages.title: Ground floor and third floor
captions: First (ground) floor plan: billiard room and playroom; the garage later enlarged by one room, as noted on the survey.
Third floor plan, 1/8 inch to the foot: the third floor holds the bedrooms under the broad hipped roof.

pages.title: Raised to the second floor
pages.caption: Longitudinal section and south elevation, 1/8 inch to the foot: the living and dining rooms raised to the second floor, the roofs cantilevered far beyond the walls.

pages.title: Two slipped volumes
pages.caption: West, east and north elevations, 1/8 inch to the foot: two slipped rectangular volumes under broad hipped roofs, brick laid with raked horizontal joints.

pages.title: Divided only by the fireplace and stair
pages.text: The ground floor holds the billiard room and playroom; the second floor is one continuous living and dining space divided only by the central fireplace and stair; the third floor holds the bedrooms. Here, the dining room on the second floor.

pages.title: Fireplace and art glass
captions: Fireplace elevations, east and west, 3/8 inch to the foot: the central fireplace dividing living and dining.
Second (main) floor windows: the art-glass doors that open the living and dining rooms to the street.

pages.title: Measured in 1963
pages.text: Measured and drawn in 1963 by the Historic American Buildings Survey (Chicago Project, survey ILL-1005) under the National Park Service; sheets by Robert C. Giebner and Janis J. Erins. Scale 1/8 inch to the foot for plans, sections and elevations; 3/8 inch for the fireplace elevations.
pages.caption: Robie House windows sheet: first-floor window pattern and second-floor window details in interior view, section and exterior.

pages.statement: Study of a measured survey. Individual work, 6 weeks.
